title: Ecclesiastes 2
paragraphs: ¹ I said to myself, "Come now, let me test you with pleasure — enjoy what is good." But that too turned out to be meaningless. ² "Laughter is madness," I said, "and what does pleasure accomplish?" ³ I tried drinking wine and embracing folly while still guiding myself with wisdom, hoping to discover what is worthwhile for people to do in the brief days of their lives. ⁴ I undertook great projects: I built houses and planted vineyards. ⁵ I made gardens and parks and planted all kinds of fruit trees in them.

⁶ I made reservoirs to water forests of flourishing trees. ⁷ I bought male and female servants, and I had servants born in my house as well. I owned more cattle and flocks than anyone before me in Jerusalem. ⁸ I also amassed silver and gold and the treasure of kings and provinces. I acquired male and female singers, and all the pleasures of a man's heart. ⁹ I became greater than any who came before me in Jerusalem, and my wisdom never left me. ¹⁰ Whatever my eyes desired I did not withhold from them; I refused my heart no pleasure. My heart took delight in all my work, and this was my reward.

¹¹ But when I surveyed everything my hands had done and all I had worked so hard to achieve, I saw that it was all meaningless — a chasing after the wind. Nothing was gained under the sun. ¹² Then I turned to consider wisdom, madness, and folly — for what more can the king's successor do than what has already been done? ¹³ I found that wisdom is better than folly, as light is better than darkness. ¹⁴ The wise person has eyes in their head, while the fool walks in the dark — but I also came to understand that the same fate overtakes them both. ¹⁵ Then I said to myself, "What happens to the fool will happen to me as well. What then did I gain by being so wise?" And I said to myself that this too is meaningless.

¹⁶ There is no lasting memory of the wise any more than the fool — in the days to come, both will be forgotten. Like the fool, the wise person must die. ¹⁷ So I came to hate life, because everything done under the sun was grievous to me. It was all meaningless, a chasing after the wind. ¹⁸ I hated all the things I had toiled for under the sun, knowing I must leave them to whoever comes after me. ¹⁹ And who knows whether that person will be wise or a fool? Yet they will have control over everything I worked for under the sun. This too is meaningless. ²⁰ So my heart despaired over all my labor under the sun.

²¹ A man may labor with wisdom, knowledge, and skill — but then must leave everything to someone who did not work for it. This too is meaningless and a great evil. ²² What does anyone gain from all their labor and anxious toil under the sun? ²³ All their days are pain, their work a burden. Even at night their mind does not rest. This too is meaningless. ²⁴ There is nothing better for a person than to eat and drink and find satisfaction in their work. This too, I saw, is from the hand of God. ²⁵ For who can eat or find enjoyment apart from him?

²⁶ To the person who pleases him, God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy; but to the sinner he gives the task of gathering and accumulating, only to hand it over to the one who pleases God. This too is meaningless — a chasing after the wind.
